newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's PM warns of EU federation after EMU.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's PM warns of EU federation after EMU.

text.p: The European Union (EU) could become a federation with common fiscal policies after Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) comes into force, Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson wrote in an editorial article in a Swedish newspaper.

"The third phase of the single currency union means that the balance between the economic and political players in Europe might change," said Persson, who heads the minority Social Democrats government, in Svenska Dagbladet.
"The common, strong and independent central bank that will handle the common monetary policy on its own might lack a counterbalancing force in European fiscal policies."

Persson wants to discuss whether such a strong European central bank will mean that fiscal policies will be lifted to EU levels or if the planned stability pact will suffice to counterbalance the power of the central bank.
If fiscal policies became a union matter, the EU would become a federation, he said.
"The EU would be transformed to something completely different than the EU the Swedish people, after some agony and a long and trying debate, approved (in a 1994 referendum)," Persson said.
Persson refrained from saying whether he was for or against EMU, instead he called for a discussion about what a monetary union would really mean.
He dismissed calls by Carl Bildt, the leader of the opposition conservative party, the Moderates, to take a stand on the single currency.
The Centre Party, the government's cooperation partner, is opposed on the grounds that it will lead to a federation.
Persson said Sweden would be able to join the single currency if it wanted to as it meets the convergence criteria.
